checks_run.procedure: Judge the three D-210 open questions with a real-database probe and by reading the code. checks_run.expected: ADR-0051 §2 as amended: the rows that carry a sensitive benefit's values are absent from lists, and their item routes answer 404, for a reader who is not admitted.
checks_run.actual: (1) DEFECT: F-DG6-220 (High, mandatory). TL and AUD get 404 on the benefit but 200 on its corrective case (benefitId, lifecycle step, benefit_variance, off-track count, title, recovery plan), its transition decision (rationale, expected realization end) and its area link. The TO and the owner (the controls) see everything. The probe exits 1 by design, and only on the soft assertion stating the ADR expectation, for TL and for AUD. (2) Acceptable. GET /status-model returns aggregates only (valueState, counts) and no per-benefit facts (probe-sensitive-registers-statusmodel.log). The per-benefit ids and codes reach only the frozen closure snapshot (closure.ts benefitSnapshot) and the G6 submission snapshot (g6SnapshotOf), which are immutable evidence of a business approval. Making them differ by viewer would break the rule that gates are explicit approvals tied to evidence snapshots. They carry ids, codes and states, never values, and aggregates may include restricted records by D-195 Q3. (3) Correct and complete within its scope. Every scenario presenter (list, item, create, PATCH) filters through restrictedRecordRefs. The POST of a hidden benefit answers like an unknown benefit (422 validation.reference). The PATCH of a hidden value is already 404 through the benefitScenarioValueId guard. A scenario carries no total. The web scenario page renders rows without summing them (RegisterPages.tsx). The finance dashboard never reads scenarios. An export of a selection that includes a hidden value is refused 403. Silent omission without a label is consistent with §2's list rule, because no aggregate is shown. sensitive-reach-scenarios.test.ts passes in int-api-p6.log.
